title: Guide - A Thankful Heart - Thanks in hard seasons

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to A Thankful Heart. <short pause> This practice is called Thanks in Hard Seasons. <short pause> If giving thanks feels difficult right now, you don't have to pretend otherwise. <short pause> You are welcome here, exactly as it is.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let your body be held by whatever is under you. <short pause> You don't need to lift your face, or fix your expression. <short pause> Breathe in as gently as you can... <short pause> and as you breathe out, let yourself stop being brave for a few minutes.

Sometimes thankfulness has been handed to us like a correction. <short pause> Look on the bright side. <short pause> Others have it worse. <short pause> But the Bible never asks you to call a painful thing good. <short pause> Its people cry out, and question, and weep... <short pause> and some of them learn to give thanks with the tears still on their faces.

The prophet Habakkuk was one of them. <short pause> He begins by asking God, how long must I cry for help? <short pause> By the end of his book, he can see disaster coming, and his whole body trembles. <short pause> And then he prays this, in chapter three, verses seventeen and eighteen.

Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls: <short pause> Yet I will rejoice in the Lord, I will joy in the God of my salvation.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: He names every empty place. <short pause> The tree. The vine. The field. The fold. The stall. <short pause> He doesn't skip one of them to reach the joy sooner. <short pause> And then comes one small word, that carries so much weight. <short pause> Yet.

So what is your although? <short pause> Although the answer hasn't come. <short pause> Although the chair is empty, or the money is short, or the body is not healing as you hoped. <short pause> Say your own sentence quietly to God, beginning with that word. <short pause> Although...

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let that sentence stand, just as you said it. <short pause> He heard it. <short pause> You don't need to soften it, or explain it, or apologize for it. <short pause> An honest although is already a prayer... <short pause> and it is already held.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now, only if you are able, look for one thing beside it. <short pause> Not instead of it. Beside it. <short pause> A person who has stayed. <short pause> A meal you managed to eat. <short pause> An hour when the pain loosened a little. <short pause> Or simply this... that you are still here, and God is still God. <short pause> Place it softly after your although. <short pause> Yet... I thank You for this.

And if you can't find a yet today, that is all right. <short pause> Habakkuk had a whole book of questions before he reached his. <short pause> Until yours comes, you can borrow his. <short pause> God is not waiting for your thanks before He will stay close to you.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: In winter, an orchard can look as if it has nothing to give. <short pause> Bare branches, hard ground, no color anywhere. <short pause> No one would ask it for fruit. <short pause> It is enough, in that season, for the roots to hold. <short pause> Your thanks may be like a root just now... small, and hidden, and holding on.

Let's pray. <short pause> God of my salvation, <short pause> You see every empty place I have named. <short pause> I will not call them good. <short pause> But I will call You good, as well as I am able. <short pause> Receive the small thanks I have, and carry me where I have none. <short pause> And where I need help, send me people to help me. <short pause> Amen.

Take one word with you into the rest of this season. <short pause> You don't have to say it loudly. <short pause> It can be a whisper, with everything still unfinished... <short pause> yet. <short pause> Go gently. You are not walking through it alone.
